newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares flat, seen up on Wednesday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares flat, seen up on Wednesday.

text.p: Polish shares were virtually flat on Tuesday after a three-day fall and analysts said the market should rebound on Wednesday in an upward correction.

"There should be a rise on Wednesday but there's no chance for big gains due to the uncertain situation outside the bourse....It's not known what will happen with inflation," said Bogdan Kornacki of Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy SA (WBK) house.

Analysts said the main market, currently at 14,913.5 points, could rise toward 15,500 before falling again on uncertainty linked with September's parliamentary elections and macreconomic concerns such as possible higher inflation.

They said recent growth of money supply aggregates have caused inflationary fears and led the central bank to increase market interest rates in the last week. On Tuesday the bank increased its benchmark 14-day rate by 0.42 to 23.00 percent.

The government is also expected to borrow as much as 2.5 billion zlotys ($721 million) from the central bank due to the recent flooding which German re-insurer Munich Re on Tuesday estimated had caused three to five billion marks in damage.

The main market's all-share WIG index slipped 6.6 points to 14,913.5 and turnover rose 6.7 percent to 152.9 million zlotys ($44.1 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 51 to 40 with 14 stocks flat.
Builder Budimex on Tuesday fell at or near the daily maximum 10 percent for the third session running on Thursday's news it revised down its 1997 pre-tax profit view.

Garment maker Prochnik surged 9.9 percent on the back of its speculative plunge on last week's news the Securities Commission told the prosecutor a group of investors may have illegally manipulated prices.
